finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint sends a GET to an attacker-supplied URL. Its only host check is a suffix match (endswith('example.com')) with no leading dot, so attacker-owned hosts such as evil-example.com pass the check and can point at internal or metadata addresses. Only len(r.text) is returned, so this is a partial, length-only read. Severity MEDIUM.
finding.sink: mirror.py:16 — httpx AsyncClient.get(url) using the full attacker-supplied URL

finding.guards_checked: Hostname parsing via .hostname (sound). Suffix-only allowlist (bypassable; ALLOWED_SUFFIX at line 7 is defined but unused). Scheme not restricted, but httpx only handles http/https. Redirects not followed (httpx AsyncClient default follow_redirects=False), so redirect check does not apply. No resolved-IP or private/loopback/metadata blocking. No authentication on the endpoint. /ping (lines 20-24) uses a hardcoded URL and is not a finding.
